headline: SEC Witness Says Records Listed Sara Duterte as Company Director Through 2025
seoTitle: SEC Records Put Sara Duterte on Company Board Through 2025, Witness Says | FMB News
seoDescription: SEC director Gerardo del Rosario testified that filings listed Sara Duterte as a Metro City Chow Foods director through 2025; the defense disputed parts of the prosecution’s presentation.
deck: SEC director Gerardo del Rosario testified that corporate filings listed Vice President Sara Duterte on Metro City Chow Foods’ board through 2025. The testimony is evidence before the impeachment court, not a finding of constitutional guilt.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Securities and Exchange Commission Company Registration and Monitoring Department director Gerardo del Rosario testified on Day 27 of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial that General Information Sheets filed by Metro City Chow Foods Corporation listed Duterte as a member of its board of directors from 2022 through 2025.

The testimony was given as the House prosecution presented corporate records under Article II of the impeachment complaint, which contains allegations involving unexplained wealth, disclosure and continued business interests.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The confirmed fact at this stage is the testimony and the SEC records as described in open court. Philippine News Agency documented Del Rosario testifying before the Senate impeachment court on September 21, while GMA News and News5 independently reported his account of the company filings.

Del Rosario also discussed Article VII, Section 13 of the 1987 Constitution, which restricts the President, Vice President and specified executive officials from participating in business during their tenure.

sections.heading: What is disputed
paragraphs: The defense objected to aspects of an SEC-prepared summary and argued that corporate authorized capital, subscribed capital and paid-up amounts should not be presented as though they were Duterte's personal holdings. Presiding officer Francis Escudero instructed the prosecution to distinguish corporate totals from Duterte's individual interests and allowed the presentation to continue with those distinctions.

No finding of guilt follows automatically from the SEC testimony. Whether the evidence establishes the allegations in Article II, whether any conduct violated the Constitution, and whether it meets the standard for impeachment conviction remain questions for the Senate impeachment court.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: This report continues FMB News' September 15 coverage of the SALN evidence in Day 25 of the trial. Earliest relevant FMB News report: /news/sara-duterte-impeachment-saln-day-25-september-15-2026.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The testimony moves the trial from the contents of Duterte's SALNs into corporate filings that the prosecution says bear on whether she continued business participation while serving as vice president. The defense's objections also sharpen the distinction between a corporation's finances and an individual's ownership or financial interest.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the defense cross-examination of Del Rosario, the impeachment court's treatment of the disputed corporate documents, and additional prosecution evidence under Article II. Any legal conclusion should be based on the full evidentiary record rather than the prosecution or defense characterization alone.

The defense position and presiding officer's response are included so corporate totals are not misrepresented as Duterte's personal holdings.
The article treats Article II claims as allegations and the testimony as evidence, not as a Senate finding of guilt or a final constitutional determination.
